item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Ryan is packing books into a rectangular box.

All the books are the same size.

[Image: A book and a box. The book measures 20 centimeters by 15 centimeters by 6 centimeters. The box has a length of 36 centimeters, width of 30 centimeters, and height of 20 centimeters.]

What is the largest number of books that will fit inside the box?

Answer: ____

descriptors: Incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

item.figure_description:
Two 3-dimensional diagrams:
1. A closed rectangular book labeled "Book" with dimensions indicated by double-headed arrows: height/thickness 6 cm, length 20 cm along the left edge, and width 15 cm along the right-front edge.
2. An open rectangular box labeled "Box" with dimensions indicated by double-headed arrows: width 30 cm along the front-left top edge, length 36 cm along the back-right top edge, and vertical height/depth of 20 cm along the inside back corner from top to bottom.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.
